messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — seeing a sudden spike of 502s for tenant acme-inc on hosted API. Started at ~08:12 UTC, ~20 errors/min. Samples attached (trace ids: 6f4a1e, 6f4a2b).
Maria Gomez: Confirmed. Envoy upstream resets and some NGINX 502s. No obvious code change. Lots of keepalive timeouts in frontdoor logs.
Samir Patel: Running a quick curl against frontdoor with tenant headers now.
Samir Patel: ```curl -v -H 'Host: hosted.redwood.ai' -H 'X-Tenant: acme-inc' 'https://gw.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
* Connected to gw.redwood.ai (10.0.0.23) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: gw.redwood.ai
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: 6f4a1e
{\"error\":\"upstream reset\"}
```
Leo Thompson: Pasted a short grep from midfront logs: 
```
midfront-1 log: http2 stream reset code=ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM conn_window_exhausted tenant=acme-inc authcache_miss=true
```
Looks like authcache miss + long-lived streams -> conn window exhaustion and envoy resets.
Alex Chen: Is this related to recent authcache TTL change rolled last night?
Maria Gomez: TTL was bumped from 30s -> 2m for authcache to reduce calls. That should reduce upstream churn, not cause keepalive churn though. But I see authcache failures for acme-inc (lots of 5xx from auth service) around same time.
Samir Patel: Correlation: auth service returned 500 for 08:11:58-08:12:20 for several tenant keys. Frontdoor retried, fanout increased, midfront connection window hit ceiling and started resetting.
support-bot: Created incident INC-2024-042 (priority: high) — notifying eng-sre.
Leo Thompson: Short mitigation applied: enabled routing fallback to the compact model variant (model-compact-v2) for acme-inc via rlb override. That reduces fanout and shortens stream lifetime. Errors dropped to ~2/min after config flip.
Alex Chen: Good. Can we get repro steps for product team?
Maria Gomez: Repro steps: 1) Make concurrent streaming requests with tenant header for acme-inc 2) Force auth service to return 500 for TTL window 3) Observe midfront logs for connwindow_exhausted 4) Observe 502s on gateway.
Samir Patel: Repro command snippet: 
```
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -s -H 'X-Tenant: acme-inc' -H 'Expect: 100-continue' https://gw.redwood.ai/v1/stream &
done
# then flip auth to error mode
```
(Use small payloads to keep connections open).
Leo Thompson: Proposed long-term fix: make authcache fallback more resilient (graceful cached miss with stale-while-revalidate), reduce per-host concurrent stream cap on midfront, and add circuit-breaker early ejection to avoid cascade. I'll open PRs for midfront and routing config.
Alex Chen: Can we also add a quick synthetic check for auth service errors and auto-roll a routing fallback if error rate > 5% in 1m for tenant?
Samir Patel: Yep — I can wire a temporary zap alert that auto-flips rlb for affected tenant for 5m.
Maria Gomez: Customer comms: sent acme-inc update: "We've applied a temporary routing fallback which reduced errors. Engineering is implementing a fix and we'll follow up with timeline."
support-bot: Incident INC-2024-042 updated: mitigation applied, next update in 30m.
Alex Chen: Thanks team. Please paste PR links and postmortem when available.
Leo Thompson: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/midfront/merge_requests/412 — includes reduced conn cap + early eject.
Samir Patel: Alert runbook notes added to #runbooks/edge-authcache.
Maria Gomez: Action items: 1) roll midfront patch (Leo) 2) authcache S-W-R implementation (Samir) 3) synth alert + auto-fallback (Alex) 4) customer postmortem (support).
Alex Chen: Closing loop: errors back to baseline after mitigation, leaving incident open for next 24h for monitoring. :white_check_mark:
support-bot: Reaction :thumbsup: from 4 users
